title: The genus-two SU(2) WRT module at level p=2*r1*r2 is irreducible when r1,r2 are distinct odd primes and the specified even CRT color x satisfies 3*x>p-4
author: Julien Korinman
work: Decomposition of some Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev Representations into Irreducible Factors
source_version: Official SIGMA 15 (2019) article 011, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2019.011; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The new obstacle is that distinct admissible colors can share Dehn-twist eigenvalues at a composite level, so the prime-level irreducibility argument does not transfer directly. The author establishes vacuum cyclicity through tensor Vandermonde separation and bounds the commutant using two banded-graph bases. An explicit genus-one swapping operator lifts to commuting handle operators whose squared action rules out the remaining nonscalar commutant direction.

proof_review.note: The complete proof of Theorem1.1(4) was read, including genus-one vacuum cyclicity, the genus-two transfer and full Vandermonde cyclicity argument (Section3), the commutant injection via the cyclic vacuum, and the actual genus-two graph and swapping-operator argument in Section4.2. Select the explicitly stated branch 3*x>2*r1*r2-4: the triple (x,x,x) is not admissible, so Lemma4.4 uses its first explicit case and does not need the separate polynomial 6j nonvanishing Lemma4.3. The latter branch proof was also read but is not selected. Established WRT skein basis, fusion rule and Weil decomposition are author-cited background. No higher-genus numerical 6j verification, other prime-level variants, or finite-group reducibility theorem is selected.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the second hypothesis branch of Theorem1.1(4): genus g=2, SU(2) WRT complex module V_p(Sigma_2) for the stated central extension of the mapping class group, p=2*r1*r2 with distinct odd primes r1,r2. The even x in {1,...,r1*r2-2} is the unique color satisfying either x=0 mod r1 and x=-2 mod r2, or the swapped pair. Require 3*x>p-4; equivalently the triple (x,x,x) fails the displayed p-admissibility sum bound. The conclusion is simplicity/irreducibility of this genus-two module. Neither the separate r1,r2>37 polynomial-nonvanishing branch nor higher-genus, prime-square or 4r statements are selected.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Partial theorem selection is explicit: only Theorem1.1(4) under 3*x>p-4. This avoids importing Lemma4.3 as an unexplained new core; the relevant first case of Lemma4.4 is supplied directly. In Proposition3.4 the wording “independent lines” refers to rows indexed by admissible colorings of the invertible tensor Vandermonde matrix, as specified by its displayed index ranges; original wording and diagrams are retained.
